housing.summary: Bergen has a tight rental market driven by students and energy-sector workers; most listings are found on Finn.no. Rentals are typically unfurnished or semi-furnished, and landlords generally require a deposit held in a separate tenancy deposit account (depositumskonto).

banking.summary: To open a Norwegian bank account you generally need a D-number or national identity number (fodselsnummer), valid ID/passport, and proof of address or an employment contract. Common banks in Bergen include DNB, Nordea, and the regional Sparebanken Vest, which is headquartered in Bergen.
required_docs: Employment contract or proof of income

schools.summary: Bergen offers Norwegian public schooling (free, tuition-funded by residence) as well as international options; the International School of Bergen provides an English-language IB-oriented curriculum for expat families.

legal_admin.summary: New arrivals must legalise their stay (EU/EEA nationals register with the police; non-EEA nationals apply for a residence permit via UDI), then register with the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret) administered by the Norwegian Tax Administration to obtain a national identity number.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence with the police/UDI, then register at the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret) via Skatteetaten to obtain a D-number or national identity number

tax_finance.summary: Residents need a tax deduction card (skattekort) from the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten). A D-number is issued for temporary stays and a national identity number (fodselsnummer) for those registered as residents.

transport.summary: Public transport in Bergen is run by Skyss and includes the Bybanen light rail, buses, and city ferries. Tickets and monthly passes are managed via the Skyss app or travel card. EU/EEA driving licences can generally be used or exchanged without a test; healthcare access requires registering with a regular GP (fastlege).
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences can be used and exchanged without a test; non-EEA licences must usually be exchanged within one year, sometimes requiring a driving test
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with a regular GP (fastlege) through HELFO once a national identity number is issued
